prompt: Review this change before it merges. The change is the single commit at HEAD of this checkout, a Rust workspace. Get the diff with `git diff HEAD~1 HEAD`. Its title is "feat(commit): draft the commit message with haiku". It makes the commit command ask a model to draft the commit message from the staged diff. Review only this checkout at HEAD. Do not build or run tests. Reply with the full review report.

expected.text: The existing integration tests for the commit command (crates/cli/tests/commit_cli.rs) run the command with no message and do not stub the claude binary or switch the new setting off, so they now call the real claude program.

The trailer check on the model's body (the TRAILER pattern in crates/cli/src/commit/model.rs) needs whitespace after the colon, so a line such as `Signed-off-by:Name` with no space passes validation and a model-written trailer reaches the commit.
The staged diff is sent to the model with no filter for secret files such as .env or key files, and -A stages everything first.
docs/guides/02-review-and-pr-flow.md still says the commit message is drafted from the staged files with no model, which is now false.
Model-written text skips the prose or writing-rules check inside validation, so a reply that passes validation can be rejected later and the commit fails with no fallback.
The forbidden-word check rejects any message that contains the bare word claude or anthropic, which legitimate commits in this repository need.
The trailer pattern treats any body line shaped like `Word: text` as a trailer, so ordinary body lines are rejected.
